title: AVA MVP Baseline With Pi And TUI Verification
fallbackReason: The Plannotator browser interview was launched and listened on http://127.0.0.1:46443, but no submitted or dismissed result was returned after repeated checks. The process was stopped and the recommended answers from interview.json were used to keep the goal setup moving.

answers.answer: Start with TUI/frontend MVP gaps because that is the current product push, but keep the full Pi-first MVP baseline as the governing checklist. Backend/RPC/session/provider/tool work remains in scope whenever a TUI feature needs a safe contract behind it.
Treat P0 and P1 as implementation scope. P2/research items should be compared against Pi/OpenCode only when useful, then documented as deferred unless a P0/P1 feature depends on them.

Require deterministic CTest coverage for renderer/editor/state logic, plus PTY or tmux-backed smoke tests for real terminal behavior whenever a TUI change affects full-screen interaction. If a real terminal smoke cannot run in the environment, the blocker and exact command must be documented before handoff.

Use Pi as the primary behavior and capability reference, especially docs/reference-code/pi/packages/coding-agent and docs/reference-code/pi/packages/tui. Do not copy Pi source or architecture; implement AVA-native C++23 modules and document any MVP exclusions.

Make optional-environment checks explicit and credential/tool-gated. The agent must run them when prerequisites are present, skip with a clear reason when they are absent, and always run normal CMake tests plus git diff checks before handoff.
